root.name: Modern Defense: Modern Pterodactyl
root.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5

overview: Black hits d4 at once with ...c5, and after 4.Nf3 cxd4 5.Nxd4 plays ...Qa5 or ...Nf6, using the early queen to hit e4 and c3. White gets space and a lead in development and tries to exploit the queen's position, while Black plays for counterplay on the dark squares and c-file. The position is unbalanced and not especially solid.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, Be2 or Bd3 and O-O, defending e4 and developing with tempo on the queen
Use the extra space and aim for a kingside initiative

black_ideas.idea: Put pressure on e4 and c3 with ...Qa5 and ...Nf6, then ...O-O
Use the half-open c-file and the g7 bishop to counter on the dark squares

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian-style asymmetric centre with Black's g7 bishop and an early queen on a5

character.notes: Unbalanced: White gets a lead and space, Black counters with the early queen; both sides can go wrong quickly.

gambit.notes: No material offered; 4.dxc5 Qa5 regains the pawn.

soundness.notes: Slightly inferior for Black but sound enough for strong players.

structure.notes: Half-open c-file after ...cxd4 and a Sicilian-type centre.

approach.notes: Played now and then, but strong players hardly choose it as a main weapon.

level.notes: Black needs to handle the early queen and e4 pressure; little long theory.

character.reason: Early queen and a lead for White make for unbalanced play.

soundness.reason: Slightly worse for Black but playable.

structure.reason: Sicilian-type asymmetric centre with a half-open c-file.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Pterodactyl.

level.reason: Clear ideas but the early queen needs care.

plans.reason: Black plays ...Qa5 early and fianchettoes the bishop on g7.
